title: Compute in memory
summary: An analog crossbar multiplies with Ohm's law where the weights live. Trade precision for energy.

ideas.how: the math happens inside the memory, so the weights never move
Ohm's law multiplies and the wires add the currents

tradeoffs.how: analog math saves energy but adds noise to every answer

measures.how: analog arrays promise much more of it

then: Memory only stores; all computing happens in the processor.
Memristors (2008) and analog memory arrays multiply in the lab.
The first analog in-memory AI chips ship for laptops and edge devices.
Projection: compute-in-memory spreads in edge AI if precision and drift are tamed.

challenges.title: Fewest bits that still work
challenges.task: Find the cheapest converter that keeps an analog crossbar within 5% of exact.

ask: Why are analog chips less precise?
